chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Action accompanied by fear for Allāh does not fail, and how can a thing fail that has been accepted.

key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness or piety, the state of guarding oneself against divine displeasure
key_terms.عَمَلٌ: Action or deed, referring to religious or moral acts
key_terms.يُقَبَّلُ: Accepted, referring to divine acceptance of a deed

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of taqwa in ensuring the acceptance of good deeds?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes taqwa as the essential quality that guarantees the acceptance (qabul) of deeds, rendering them never insignificant. The rhetorical question underscores the logical certainty that if God has accepted an action, it cannot be diminished or rejected, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual quality of piety over mere quantity of worship. This reflects the broader theological principle that sincerity and God-consciousness are the true measures of a deed's value in the sight of the Divine.
